classification.difficultyReason: Translate six supplied inequalities directly into rays or intervals, distinguishing open and closed endpoints.

content.prompt: Graph each set of real numbers on a number line.

answer.short: Open endpoint at $1$; ray to the right.
answer.worked: Mark $1$ with an open circle because $1$ is excluded. Draw a ray to the right for values greater than $1$.

spec.description: Number-line template cannot specify a straight solution ray separately from its axis; native TikZ retains the open endpoint and rightward solution arrow.

answer.short: Closed endpoint at $2$; ray to the left.
answer.worked: Mark $2$ with a closed circle because $2$ is included. Draw a ray to the left for values less than or equal to $2$.

spec.description: Native TikZ expresses the straight leftward solution ray separately from the number-line axis.

answer.short: Closed endpoint at $-3$; ray to the right.
answer.worked: Mark $-3$ with a closed circle because $-3$ is included. Draw a ray to the right for values greater than or equal to $-3$.

spec.description: Native TikZ expresses the straight rightward solution ray separately from the number-line axis.

answer.short: Open endpoints at $0$ and $3$; join them with a segment.
answer.worked: Both inequalities are strict, so mark $0$ and $3$ with open circles. Join them to represent every value between $0$ and $3$.

spec.description: Native TikZ expresses the straight interval segment separately from the number-line axis; the template has no interval-segment field.

answer.short: Open endpoint at $-2$, closed endpoint at $1$; join them with a segment.
answer.worked: Mark $-2$ with an open circle and $1$ with a closed circle. Join them to represent all values greater than $-2$ and less than or equal to $1$.

spec.description: Native TikZ retains the interval segment, mixed endpoint inclusion and the source-labelled zero tick.

answer.short: Closed endpoint at $-5$, open endpoint at $10$; join them with a segment.
answer.worked: Mark $-5$ with a closed circle and $10$ with an open circle. Join them to represent all values greater than or equal to $-5$ and less than $10$.

spec.description: Native TikZ retains the interval segment, mixed endpoint inclusion and the source-labelled zero tick with a uniform numerical scale.
